gate: Every tier 1 and tier 1b feature passes on each surface that applies, and so does every acceptance criterion of their stories. This includes N1 to N4, so the UI consolidation is part of this release. Deferred only with a written reason.
Tier 2 should work: an open item does not block the release, but the changelog names it as a known gap. Tier 3 may wait.
Every requirement is met, or deferred with a reason. Outdated ones are rewritten.
Every finding is fixed, or accepted with a reason. Accepted limits are stated in the README.
The automated suites and `claude plugin validate` pass, and a manual run is recorded on all three surfaces.
Real use is recorded: the author's own paper for at least 2 weeks, and a think-aloud with 2 to 3 researchers.

findings.note: Guard built and confirmed in a real session on 2026-11-05 (F15). Remaining limits are in the README

findings.why: R1.1 and R1.4 depend on model behaviour, which has no tests today
findings.note: Decided by the author, 2026-11-05: marker only, no guess-based detector. 9 of 9 clean on Haiku. The limit is in the README

findings.title: No warning for confidential material: only a rule line in the workspace `CLAUDE.md` exists
findings.evidence: Search over hooks, tools and template
findings.note: Deferred by the author past 0.4.0: no new features before it. The README says there is no warning

findings.note: Deferred by the author past 0.4.0: no new features before it. The README says there are no templates

findings.title: Two requirements are out of date: R1.3 forbids corrected sentences, R2.2 lets Claude write to `literature/`
findings.note: R1.3 and R2.2 rewritten to match the product

findings.title: The README overstates "read-only": each persona is called a read-only subagent, but 3 have Write and 3 have Bash
findings.why: Doc fix, and the guard must hold for these personas
findings.note: The README now says which personas can write notes or use the shell; the guard held for them in hook tests and real session g5

findings.title: Skill text has almost no automated coverage: 9 of the 11 skills checked are not named in the hook tests (`ailog.py` itself is tested)
findings.evidence: Search by name in `plugin/tests/cowriting.test.tsx`; a rough check
findings.why: These are the instructions behind most of the help the author sees

findings.title: Small doc gaps: `/cowrite:paper versioning` is missing from the skill's hint and description; the README command table omits `m` (Remember)
findings.note: The skill's hint names versioning; the README table names m

findings.title: The guard refuses harmless shell commands. Reproduced inside a paper: `cp manuscript/main.md notes/ai/copy.md`, `pandoc manuscript/main.md -o notes/ai/out.html` and a `python3 -c` that only reads and prints all only read the manuscript. Outside any paper it also refused commands whose text merely named the folder, including a prompt passed to a script; the exact trigger there is not pinned down
findings.evidence: `dev/attacks/g4-false-alarms.txt`, run 2026-11-05: 3 of 10 harmless steps refused. The README already names the `cp` case as a known limit of the pattern check
findings.why: False alarms teach authors and Claude to work around the guard, and they now also appear in the disclosure's list of refused attempts
findings.note: The guard now reads where a command writes. Real session g4: all harmless commands pass. Remaining limit: a write it cannot place is refused inside a paper if the command names a protected file

findings.title: Refused attempts leave no trace: a refused write to the log or the author's files is not logged, and a refused tool is missing from the response's `tools_used`. The disclosure's heading *Attempts to change the AI log afterwards* therefore lists only rewrites that got through
findings.evidence: Real session on 2026-11-05: steps 1 and 2 were refused, and the log has one guard entry (step 4) and `tools_used: ["Bash"]`
findings.why: The author signs this. Either log refusals too, or word the heading so it does not read as complete
findings.note: Refusals logged and listed under their own heading; confirmed in a real session: 17 attempts, 17 entries, stats shows 0 changes

findings.title: A new file can still be created in the log: `L=ai; echo S11 > "${L}-log/forged.jsonl"` passed, because the pattern can't read the variable and the comparison treats a new file as growth. It is not shown or disclosed
findings.evidence: `dev/attacks/g2-hidden-writes.txt`, step 11, run 2026-11-05; `ailog.py stats` skipped the invalid line silently
findings.why: A whole forged file would feed the disclosure. The author asked for the log to be guarded from anything but append
findings.note: New files in the log are taken out, kept and recorded. Hook test only: real case g2 has not reached the guard yet

findings.title: Persona reports may not count as turns: a headless session with 5 subagents logged 6 prompts and 1 response, and `ailog.py stats` shows Turns: 1. If this also holds in an interactive session, those reports never ask for a classification and are missing from the disclosure's counts. Not yet confirmed there
findings.evidence: `dev/attacks/g5-subagents.txt`, run 2026-11-05; the existing hook test covers one summoned persona only
findings.why: S2 needs every AI input on the record. To check under test type E, in an interactive session
findings.note: Every report keeps its turn. Hook test and a real headless session g5; an interactive session is still to check

findings.title: The guard reached beyond papers: any folder with a `paper.json` counted as a paper, so all its files were refused; outside a paper, commands naming the folder next to a variable or substitution were refused; with a paper open, another folder's own files were refused by name
findings.evidence: Seen when the guard refused commands in this plugin's own repository, 2026-11-05; `findPaper` and `bashHitsPaperManuscript` in `plugin/hooks/register.tsx`
findings.why: The plugin is usually installed for every folder, so this would regularly block other projects
findings.note: A paper needs its workspace folders; outside a paper only visible paper paths count. Real sessions g6 and g7 pass, hook tests cover the rest. The price is in the README

findings.title: A decision can be recorded blind: at 48x24 the pane shows only its header and no feedback, yet pressing o and then a records the input as adopted
findings.evidence: `scripts/screen_suite.py`, first seen 2026-11-05 in a real terminal; the simulated engine has no notion of the pane's height
findings.why: The author signs a record of what they did with each input. A key press on something unseen makes it untrue
findings.note: Small windows show the choices before anything else; too small to show them, no key can decide and the pane says so. Real terminal, screen suite at 48x24 and 44x16

findings.title: At 48 columns the tab strip breaks a label across lines, and the row beside it pushes the letters out of place (`[ S`, then `ope`)
findings.evidence: `scripts/screen_suite.py`; the 0.2 changelog says the pane was read at 48 columns, but through the harness, not a terminal
findings.why: The README promises the pane works in the terminal, and a narrow split is common
findings.note: Narrow, the open tab shows its name and the others their numbers. Real terminal. The refresh button is still clipped at 48 columns; its key works

findings.title: In the opened view the report is below the fold at 100x40 with no hint that it is there, and scrolling to it takes the choices off screen. The pane uses about a third of the free height. Keys it doesn't handle go to the prompt box
findings.evidence: Real terminal, 2026-11-05: PageDown reaches the report; `j` landed in the prompt box
findings.why: An author can decide without having read, which is S7. To solve with N1 to N4 in the UI consolidation
findings.note: The hint, the order and results above the text are built. The pane's height and keys it doesn't handle reaching the prompt box belong to Claude Code, so they stay; both are harmless

findings.title: Stale characters on screen: `The Terminologist` drew as `The Terminmlogist` at 100x40 in two runs and correctly at 120x70, `What did` as `Whet di(` after scrolling at 48x24, and at 44x16 a line of the Party tab stayed below the opened view. The plugin's text is right, so probably how the screen is redrawn
findings.evidence: tmux capture of the real pane, 2026-11-05; seen under tmux only so far
findings.why: Looks broken if authors see it too. To check in a plain terminal in the manual run
